title: Hot Cocoa Mix

drivers.name: 25% off promotion
drivers.evidence: 2026-01-19: 30% off → x1.18; past 10% & 25% promos had noise-adjusted lift x1.02; deeper discount justifies higher lift, but shrink due to noise and weak recent trend.

adjustment.analysis: The 25% off promotion is deeper than past 10% or 25% discounts (2025-12-15), which had noise-adjusted lifts of x1.02. The 30% off in 2026-01-19 saw x1.18, but that week had strong holiday demand. Recent weeks show low sales (23–26 units) post-Easter, suggesting demand is soft. The classical model’s x1.02 is too low—evidence from a deeper discount (30% off) and current weak trend justifies higher lift. However, the promotion is not on a holiday, and the past 10% promo lift was noise-adjusted to x1.02. Shrink toward 1.0 due to thin evidence and noise. Downside risk from recent sales dip and post-promo drop (x0.78) is muted by strong discount. Final median adjusted up, but conservatively.

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-44% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
